> **Example.** You could push a loaded cart by hand. Using a First Form that genuinely helps, you get +1 on the attempt.

Leverage is **not added to every magical roll.** Most of the time, what magic gives you is the chance to try something nobody else could. The bonus is only for magic that helps with something you could already do.

### Cost in Word Stress

Every Form has a **cost**: the number of boxes it marks on **each** of its Words when you cast it. The cost is recorded with the Form (most early Forms cost 1). A Second Form with cost 1 marks one box on each of its two Words.

- **Where the boxes come from:** a Word you manifested, or a Resource's Word. When all of a Word's boxes are marked, it is gone.
- **Runes are different:** a Rune pays the whole cost of **one** cast, then goes inert (see [Runes](game.html#post-runes)).

**Bigger effects.** You may mark **extra boxes** when you cast, to make the effect bigger in the fiction: each extra box buys one step of scope, such as a heavier target, a larger area, one more target or a longer-lasting effect. Extra boxes **never** add to the roll: magic's bonus stays +1, +2 or +3 (see *Permission or leverage* above).

> **Example.** With `Move □ □ □`, a Kinetic Shove on a crate marks 1 box. To shove the loaded cart behind it as well, the caster marks 1 extra: `Move ■ ■ □`.

### Early Forms are clumsy

The first Forms were discovered by trial and error, and their techniques still carry steps nobody has proven are needed. Effect Glowing was first performed with markings painted on the wrists; Simple Sauna with a symbol drawn on the floor. Some of these steps will turn out to be unnecessary, and research can show which. When it does, the Form gets easier for everyone (see [Spell Innovation](game.html#post-spell-innovation)).

### Known Forms

Every Form Endros has recorded is listed in [Spellcasting](game.html#post-spellcasting) and in [Discoveries](discoveries.html#forms).

title: Spell Innovation
summary: Magic grows through research. Base Forms and Forms are Stunts, and Downtime **Projects** are how you learn them, invent new ones and simplify old techniques. They are also how you take on questions nobody has answered yet, such as how to make a Rune.
details:
### Magical knowledge is progression

Every Base Form and every Form is a **Stunt**, and Stunts can come out of Downtime [Projects](game.html#post-projects). That makes magic part of the same system as everything else in Endros. A character becomes a better caster by:

- studying an existing Form, or reproducing a published experiment;
- learning the Base Form for a Word;
- inventing a new Form;
- improving a technique, or proving that one of its steps isn't needed;
- testing a hypothesis about how magic, or a Rune, works.

Someone who knows several Base Forms and several Forms has put real time into it.

### Learning a Base Form or a Form

To learn a Base Form or a Form, start a Project with it as the goal. Learning something already recorded is cheaper than inventing it:

| Stunt | Learn (recorded) | Invent (new) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Base Form: [Word]** | 6 Progress | — |
| **First Form** | 4 Progress | 6 Progress |
| **Second Form** | 6 Progress | 10 Progress |
| **Third Form** | 10 Progress | 15 Progress |

- The GM adds **Requirements** as usual: a spellbook or a published paper, a teacher, a source of the Word to practise with, a Facility.
- When the Project is complete, write the Stunt on your sheet. It **doesn't cost Refresh**: the Project was the price.
- Whether a Form is recorded, and so cheaper to learn, depends on who knows it and whether they share it (see *Who gets to know* below).

### Where new Forms come from

Ideas for a new Form usually start from:

- an observed Gate phenomenon;
- a Resource and its Functions;
- a Rune or another magical artifact;
- Research;
- experiment;
- existing Words and Forms.

### The Spell Innovation Project

A Spell Innovation Project is a normal Project whose goal is a new Form: a reliable, repeatable technique that uses Words in a new way. Its size follows the table above (6, 10 or 15 Progress by tier). When it's done, the GM records the new Form with its Words, effect and cost. A typical path:

1. Pick the effect you want.
2. Work out which Word, or Words, could produce it.
3. Get access to those Words.
4. Form a hypothesis for the technique.
5. Run the Project: test the Form, and deal with experimental Complications.
6. When it's complete, the new Form is recorded as a repeatable Stunt.

> **Known Words:** `Heat`, `Invert`
> **Proposed Form:** *Flash Freeze*, which turns a target's heat into cold (the *Chill* interaction)
> **Project:** turn that theoretical interaction into a reproducible magical technique.

A Resource that shows part of the effect in nature makes a strong Requirement or starting point: Paleglass already resists changes in temperature. How Function interactions work, including dangerous combinations, is in [Resource Functions](game.html#post-resource-functions). A Form built on an unstable pair is possible, but expect harsher Complications along the way.

### Who gets to know

Once a new Form exists, it becomes part of what the world knows about magic. Whether it stays private, is shared with a sponsor, is kept restricted or is published for everyone is a choice with consequences in the fiction. The University of Verna, the Vesper Republic and the other powers have very different views on it.

### Making magic easier

Casting today is slow, book-bound and full of steps nobody has proven are needed. Research can change that, for everyone who comes after. Projects might produce:

- simpler equations, better notation, standard tables or memory techniques;
- instruments that help with the calculation;
- substitutes for the spoken sound, or simpler gestures;
- proof that a step in an early Form (such as Effect Glowing's wrist markings) can be dropped;
- ways to store a Word for later.

Breakthroughs like these are discoveries the campaign makes in play. They aren't assumed from the start.

### Rune research

Nobody knows how to make a [Rune](game.html#post-runes). Working that out is one of the great open problems of the age, and it's open to players:

1. Gather observations of Runes.
2. Compare them with the known Words.
3. Research for clues.
4. Propose a hypothesis for how a particular Rune works.
5. Start a Project to reproduce it, and test the hypothesis.

Research is rewarded, not blind guessing. A wrong hypothesis can still rule out possibilities, reveal part of the answer, produce an unexpected result, create a Complication, reveal a missing Requirement or raise a new question.

title: Outpost Capabilities
summary: Capabilities describe what Endros can reliably support as a settlement. Each has a rating on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html), and a Capability can add Progress when the settlement's people, tools or expertise genuinely help your Project.
details:
### The six Capabilities

| Capability | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| **Industry** | Crafting, repairs and manufacturing. |
| **Research** | Investigation, analysis and Gate knowledge. |
| **Commerce** | Trade, funding and access to resources. |
| **Security** | Defense, policing and emergency response. |
| **Medicine** | Treatment and recovery. |
| **Infrastructure** | Facilities, transportation and services. |

The Outpost Sheet also lists the Facilities and characters behind each Capability: the workshops, laboratories and docks that do the work.

### Capabilities in Project Actions

When you make a Project Action (see [Projects](game.html#post-projects)), you may **spend 1 extra Downtime** to have one relevant Capability **add its rating to the Progress you gain**, as long as the settlement is actually helping you.

- Rebuilding an engine in the Workshops: **Industry** helps.
- Rebuilding it alone in a tent at the edge of a Gate: Industry probably doesn't help.

A Capability isn't an automatic solution. You still describe what your character is doing and roll a Skill. The Capability adds to the result. Only one Capability can support each Project Action, and the extra Downtime doesn't count as a second action on the Project.

> **Example.** Mira studies a preserved Gate organism in the University laboratories. She spends 2 Downtime: 1 for the action and 1 for the laboratory's help. She rolls Lore and succeeds for 2 Progress, then adds Endros's Research rating because the laboratory's equipment and staff are part of her approach.

### Capabilities as Requirements

Advanced Projects may need a Capability at a certain rating before they can start or finish. For example, a surgical procedure on a Gate-touched patient might need a certain level of Medicine. See [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications).

### Improving Capabilities

Capabilities can change over time. Facilities and completed Projects can improve them, and Outpost Consequences can strain them. See [Facilities & Outpost Development](game.html#post-facilities-and-outpost-development).

title: Facilities & Outpost Development
summary: A Facility is a permanent addition to Endros, such as a laboratory, hospital wing or workshop, and it is usually built through a **Public Project** that many characters work on across many expeditions.
details:
### How a Facility gets built

1. **Someone proposes it** and explains what it is for.
2. **The GM defines its Completion Effect**: what Endros can do once it exists.
3. **Requirements are set** (see [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications)).
4. **Players spend Downtime** on Project Actions (see [Projects](game.html#post-projects)).
5. **Missing Requirements** may lead to Research or expedition objectives.
6. **When the Project is complete**, the Facility joins Endros and appears on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html).

### What Facilities do

Facilities should mostly create **new possibilities** rather than just add numbers. A Facility might:

- unlock new kinds of Project;
- allow safe work with dangerous materials;
- meet Requirements for other Projects;
- unlock new Marketplace items;
- offer special Preparation actions before expeditions;
- make recovery possible for certain Consequences;
- improve or expand an Outpost Capability (see [Outpost Capabilities](game.html#post-outpost-capabilities));
- allow Research that was impossible before.

> **Example: a Containment Laboratory.**
> - **Proposed because:** nobody can safely study Resources that combine `Catalyze` and `Release`. Two samples have already exploded in the University.
> - **Type:** Public Project (Facility), Major, about 10 Progress
> - **Requirements:** Research at a set rating; a shielding material with `Stabilize` and either `Dampen` or `Nullify`; a qualified overseer
> - **Completion Effect:** Projects that handle unstable Resources can be worked on safely in Endros, and it adds a Research Capability asset.

### A shared achievement

Because a Public Project is open to everyone, a Facility is usually built by many players over several expeditions. One character proposes it, another crew brings back the shielding, and someone who has missed three sessions spends their extra Downtime finishing it. Whoever completes it, the result is part of Endros for every crew that follows.

title: Marketplace Development
summary: A **Marketplace Project** is Endros learning to reliably make, acquire or distribute an item. When it is finished, the item appears in the [Marketplace](marketplace.html) and any Expeditioner can get it there.

title: Rules at a Glance
summary: Every mechanic on one page, with no explanations. Cards marked **House rule** are this campaign's changes to Fate Core.
details:
Full rules are in the learning paths. Every Skill: [Skill List](game.html#post-skill-list).

## Rolling

### The roll

- Roll **4 Fate dice** (each −1, 0 or +1) and add your **Skill**.
- Add **+2** for each Aspect you invoke.
- Compare with the **difficulty** or the opposing roll. Each point of difference is a **shift**.

### The ladder

| | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| +8 | Legendary | +2 | Fair |
| +7 | Epic | +1 | Average |
| +6 | Fantastic | +0 | Mediocre |
| +5 | Superb | −1 | Poor |
| +4 | Great | −2 | Terrible |
| +3 | Good | | |

### Outcomes

| Result | Shifts |
| --- | --- |
| **Fail** | below the target |
| **Tie** | 0 |
| **Success** | 1–2 |
| **Success with Style** | 3 or more |

### Teamwork

- Each helper with the Skill at Average (+1) or better: **+1** to the roller.
- Helpers share the roller's costs and consequences.

## Actions

### Overcome

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Fail | Fail, or succeed at a serious cost. |
| Tie | Succeed at a minor cost. |
| Success | Succeed. |
| With Style | Succeed and gain a **boost**. |

### Create an Advantage

| | New Aspect | Existing Aspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fail | None, or it exists and the opposition gets the free invoke | Opposition gets a free invoke |
| Tie | A boost instead | 1 free invoke |
| Success | Aspect + 1 free invoke | 1 free invoke |
| With Style | Aspect + 2 free invokes | 2 free invokes |

### Attack

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Fail | No harm. |
| Tie | No harm; gain a **boost**. |
| Success | Hit for shifts in stress. |
| With Style | Hit; may reduce it by 1 for a **boost**. |

### Defend

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Fail | You take the hit. |
| Tie | Attacker gains a **boost**. |
| Success | No harm. |
| With Style | No harm; gain a **boost**. |

## Aspects & Fate Points

### Invoke

- Pay **1 Fate Point** or use a **free invoke**.
- Gain **+2**, or **reroll** all dice.
- Or add +2 to someone else's roll, or +2 to a difficulty against someone.
- Free invokes stack with each other and with paid invokes.
- A **boost** is an Aspect with one free invoke that vanishes once used.

### Compel

- Accept the complication: **gain 1 Fate Point**.
- Refuse it: **pay 1 Fate Point**.

### Fate Points & Stunts

- Start each session with Fate Points equal to your **Refresh**, or keep more if you ended the last session with more.
- New characters: Refresh **3**, **3 Stunts** free.
- Each extra Stunt costs 1 Refresh (minimum Refresh 1), except magical Stunts learned through Projects.

## Harm

### Stress

- Start with **2 Physical** and **2 Mental** boxes.
- Physique / Will: Average or Fair (+1/+2) → 3 boxes; Good or Great (+3/+4) → 4 boxes; Superb (+5)+ → 4 boxes and an extra Mild Consequence slot.
- One box per hit; a box absorbs shifts equal to its number.
- Stress clears after the scene.

### Consequences

| Severity | Absorbs |
| --- | --- |
| Mild | 2 |
| Moderate | 4 |
| Severe | 6 |

- Can't absorb the hit: **taken out**.
- **Concede** before a roll: you lose on your terms, gain 1 Fate Point + 1 per Consequence taken in the conflict.

### Recovery (House rule)

- Consequences **never** fade with time.
- A **Recovery Project** lowers one by one step: Mild 2, Moderate 4, Severe 6 Progress.
- It can only step down into a **free** slot: Severe needs a free Moderate slot, Moderate a free Mild one.
- Outpost: Low 2, Moderate 4, High 6, Critical 8 Progress; no slot limits.

### Armor (House rule)

- When you'd take Physical Stress the Armor could stop, **mark 1 Armor box** instead.
- A marked box stays marked until repaired or replaced.
- Only if the Armor was brought into action.

## Downtime & Projects

### Downtime (House rule)

| After an expedition | Gain |
| --- | --- |
| Took part | **2** |
| Stayed in Endros | **3** |

- Hold at most **8**; the rest is lost.
- Free: roleplay, conversations, buying Gear.

### Project Action (House rule)

1. Spend **1 Downtime**.
2. Describe the approach and the Skill.
3. Roll against the GM's difficulty.

| Result | Progress |
| --- | --- |
| Fail | 0 + a Complication |
| Tie | 1 |
| Success | 2 |
| With Style | 3 |

### Limits (House rule)

- **One action per Project** per character between expeditions.
- **Capability help:** when you make a Project Action, you may spend **1 extra Downtime** (2 in total) to add one relevant Outpost Capability's rating to the Progress you gain.
- The extra Downtime is part of the same action, not a second one.

### Project size (House rule)

| Size | Progress |
| --- | --- |
| Minor | ~4 |
| Standard | ~6 |
| Major | ~10 |
| Grand | 15+ or stages |

Bigger Projects need more Progress and Requirements, not higher difficulties.

### Requirements & Complications (House rule)

- Missing Requirement: Project **Paused**; Progress is kept.
- Complication: a new Aspect, a harder next step, a block, extra Progress, a new Requirement or an expedition objective.

## Gear & Coins

### Coins (House rule)

- Start with Coins = **Resources** rating (0 at +0 or lower).
- After each expedition: raise Coins to your Resources rating if below. If you took part, refresh **first**, then add rewards.
- Buying costs no Downtime.

### Packs & Carry Limit (House rule)

- One **Active Pack**. Starting Packs: Carry Limit **6**.
- Pack contents don't count toward the limit.
- Extra Gear brought into action: total weight ≤ Carry Limit + Carry modifier.
- Used-up contents stay gone until the Pack is restocked.
- Own Sponsor's Packs: 0 Coins. Others: 1 Coin.

### Forgot something? (House rule)

| Producing an owned item mid-expedition | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Stays within Carry Limit | **1 stress** |
| Goes over Carry Limit | **1 Fate Point** |

### Gear Tags (House rule)

- Tags (`Cutting`, `Loud`...) give **no numerical bonus**.
- An item can still have **Aspects** or **Stunts** tied to it, which work as usual.
- Weapons have no damage numbers; ordinary ammunition isn't counted.
- Limited supplies come in kits with their own count.

## Gates & Discoveries

### Domains (House rule)

- A Gate has one Domain (rarely two). Its Resources, creatures and hazards share it.
- A Domain gives **no bonus** by itself; Stunts, Gear and Projects refer to it.

### Resources (House rule)

| Availability | Means |
| --- | --- |
| Sample | Enough for Research |
| Limited | Enough for one Project |
| Available | Dependable supply |

- Most Resources have 1–3 Functions. Some are Hidden until Research reveals them.

### Combining Functions (House rule)

| Interaction | Difficulty |
| --- | --- |
| Synergy | Comparatively easy |
| No known relationship | Moderate, surprises likely |
| Opposition | Hard; may need extra Requirements |
| Instability | High risk |

## Spellcasting

### Getting a Word (House rule)

- **How can a Word appear in a scene?** From a **Rune**, from a Resource with that Function, from a Word someone already manifested, or by casting your own **Base Form: [Word]** Stunt.
- **What does a Base Form need?** That Word's Base Form Stunt, your spellbook, and your voice.
- **How is it resolved?** **Lore** against **Fair (+2)** (a Stunt can swap the Skill). One Word per roll:

| Result | Word Stress |
| --- | --- |
| Fail | no Word |
| Tie | 1 box |
| Success | 2 boxes |
| With Style | 3 boxes |

- **Pushing it:** once per Word, **1 Fate Point** adds your Lore rating in boxes, even on a Fail.
- **How long does a Word stay in play?** Until the **end of the scene**, or until its boxes are all marked. No limit on how many you hold.

### Runes & Resources (House rule)

- **Rune:** pays the whole cost of **one** Form cast, then goes **inert**.
- **Resource:** offers **1–4 boxes per Word** (listed in Discoveries). Casting through it: **+1 difficulty**.
- A Resource's Words clear **1 box at the end of each scene**, and fully between expeditions.

### Casting a Form (House rule)

- **Every Form is a Stunt**, learned separately.
- **How many Words does each tier need?**

| Tier | Words |
| --- | --- |
| Base Form | 1 (it creates it) |
| First Form | 1 |
| Second Form | 2 |
| Third Form | 3 |

- **What does a Form need?** All its Words available in the scene, and enough freedom to perform its physical technique.
- **How is it resolved?** Its own roll, separate from any Base Form roll. Usually Overcome.
- **What does it cost?** Mark its listed **cost** on **each** of its Words.
- **Bigger effect?** Mark extra boxes for more scope (heavier, wider, more targets, longer). Never a bonus to the roll.

### What does the magic give you? (House rule)

| Without magic, the action is… | The Form gives you |
| --- | --- |
| **Impossible** | Permission to roll at all. No bonus. |
| **Already possible** | A bonus: **+1** First Form, **+2** Second, **+3** Third. |

- Only one of the two applies to a roll.

### Learning magic (House rule)

| Stunt | Learn | Invent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base Form | 6 | — |
| First Form | 4 | 6 |
| Second Form | 6 | 10 |
| Third Form | 10 | 15 |

- Progress needed, as a Project. Magical Stunts gained this way **cost no Refresh**.

title: Skill List
summary: Nowhere Expeditions uses the standard **Fate Core** skill list: eighteen Skills, each rated on the ladder from Mediocre (+0) upward. This page lists them, says what each covers, and notes where the campaign's own rules use a particular Skill.
details:
### The skills

| Skill | What it covers | In this campaign |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Athletics** | Running, jumping, climbing, swimming, dodging; general physical agility. | Defending against physical attacks you can dodge. |
| **Burglary** | Getting past locks, alarms and security; understanding how they work. | |
| **Contacts** | Knowing people, finding the right person, hearing rumours. | |
| **Crafts** | Building, repairing, taking apart and understanding machines and objects. | Most crafting and engineering Projects. The Vardic Holds Extra uses it. |
| **Deceive** | Lying, disguise, misdirection, bluffing. | |
| **Drive** | Handling vehicles and mounts: carts, steam vehicles, boats and anything else that moves. | |
| **Empathy** | Reading people's moods and motives; noticing when someone is lying. | Who acts first in a mental conflict. |
| **Fight** | Close combat, armed or unarmed. | |
| **Investigate** | Deliberate, careful study: searching a scene, following clues, piecing evidence together. | Research Projects. |
| **Lore** | Learning and scholarship: history, science, languages, theory, the Archive. | Research Projects. Casting a Base Form. |
| **Notice** | Spotting things without looking for them; general awareness and reaction. | Who acts first in a physical conflict. |
| **Physique** | Strength, endurance and raw physical power. | Extra Physical stress boxes at higher ratings. |
| **Provoke** | Intimidating, unsettling or angering people to get a reaction. | Mental attacks. |
| **Rapport** | Making a good impression, persuading, building trust. | |
| **Resources** | Wealth, credit and access to money and materials. | Your starting Coins, and the level your Coins refresh to after each expedition. See [Coins, Marketplace & Personal Stash](game.html#post-coins-marketplace-and-personal-stash). |
| **Shoot** | Ranged weapons: firearms, bows, thrown weapons. | |
| **Stealth** | Staying hidden and moving unseen or unheard. | |
| **Will** | Mental fortitude, resisting fear, temptation and strain. | Defending against mental attacks; extra Mental stress boxes at higher ratings. |

Which Skill a Project Action uses depends on your **approach**, not on the Project. Repairing a crane might use Crafts, but persuading the dock workers to help with it uses Rapport. See [Projects](game.html#post-projects).

### The ladder

| Rating | Name |
| --- | --- |
| +8 | Legendary |
| +7 | Epic |
| +6 | Fantastic |
| +5 | Superb |
| +4 | Great |
| +3 | Good |
| +2 | Fair |
| +1 | Average |
| +0 | Mediocre |
| −1 | Poor |
| −2 | Terrible |

Any Skill you haven't rated is **Mediocre (+0)**. You can still roll it.

### Rating your skills

A new character follows the standard Fate Core arrangement:

- one Skill at **Great (+4)**;
- two at **Good (+3)**;
- three at **Fair (+2)**;
- four at **Average (+1)**.

Everything else stays at Mediocre (+0). The [character sheet](sheet.html) lists every Skill at +0 to start with.

### Skills and stress

**Physique** adds Physical stress boxes, and **Will** adds Mental ones:

| Rating | Stress boxes |
| --- | --- |
| Mediocre (+0) | 2 |
| Average (+1) or Fair (+2) | 3 |
| Good (+3) or Great (+4) | 4 |
| Superb (+5) or higher | 4, plus an extra Mild Consequence slot for that kind of harm |

### Magic and Skills

A **Base Form** is cast with **Lore**, against Fair (+2). A Stunt can let one caster use a different Skill for one Word's Base Form. A **Form**'s own roll uses whatever Skill fits the action, as with any roll. See [Base Forms](game.html#post-base-forms).
